13.5 Stage 5 — Guided “To-Do” Practice Labs
Open part_03_engineering_workflow/ch13_jupyter_colab/02_guided_todos.ipynb in Google Colab, run Step 0 to activate sharukh-tutor, and build all six notebook-engineering utilities below. Every file-based check runs inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory():

To-Do 13.1 (Hidden-State Audit — detect_out_of_order_cells(nb_dict)): Inspect code cells’ execution_count (skipping markdown cells) and return True if any code cell has execution_count is None or <= the previous executed count, else False.
To-Do 13.2 (Git Hygiene — strip_notebook_outputs(nb_dict)): Return a deep-copied clean notebook dict with outputs = [] and execution_count = None on every code cell without mutating the caller’s input dictionary.
To-Do 13.3 (Colab Launcher — build_colab_url(owner, repo, branch, rel_path)): Return the exact URL https://colab.research.google.com/github/{owner}/{repo}/blob/{branch}/{rel_path} after stripping any leading / from rel_path.
To-Do 13.4 (Portable Storage — resolve_data_path(filename, drive_dir=None, local_dir=None)): Check Path(drive_dir) / filename first, then Path(local_dir) / filename; return the first existing Path or raise FileNotFoundError.
To-Do 13.5 (Atomic Checkpointing — save_checkpoint_atomic(ckpt_path, state_dict)): Serialize state_dict as UTF-8 JSON to Path(ckpt_path).with_suffix(".tmp"), then atomically rename it onto ckpt_path via .replace().
To-Do 13.6 (Isolated Reproducibility — seeded_train_test_indices(n_samples, test_ratio=0.2, seed=42)): Use an isolated random.Random(seed) (never global random.seed()) to shuffle list(range(n_samples)) and return (train_idx, test_idx) with len(test_idx) == int(n_samples * test_ratio).

13.6 Stage 6 — Concept & Execution Trace Test (No Computer Allowed!)
Test your understanding on paper before checking Stage 8:

Hidden-State Execution Counts: A notebook has three code cells with execution_count values [1, 4, 2] and one markdown cell between them. Why is this notebook unsafe to submit as reproducible supplementary material?
Unexecuted Cell Risk: A notebook has code cells with execution_count values [1, None, 2]. What does detect_out_of_order_cells(nb_dict) return, and why?
Shallow vs. Deep Copy Bug: Why does cleaned = nb_dict.copy() fail to protect nb_dict when strip_notebook_outputs sets cell["outputs"] = []?
Colab Ephemeral Disk: You save cleaned_cohort.csv directly to /content/cleaned_cohort.csv in Google Colab, close your laptop for 3 hours, and reconnect to a new runtime. What happened to cleaned_cohort.csv?
CPU vs. GPU Discipline: Why is it poor practice to leave a Colab T4/A100 GPU runtime enabled while writing Pandas data-cleaning code and reading documentation?
Magic Syntax Error: You copy a Colab cell containing !pip install -q pandas and %timeit sum(range(1000)) straight into utils.py and run import utils. What Python exception occurs?
.replace() vs. Direct Write: Suppose train_state.json currently holds a valid epoch-10 checkpoint, and your code writes epoch 11 using save_checkpoint_atomic. If json.dump() crashes halfway through with a TypeError, what is inside train_state.json afterward?
Global vs. Isolated RNG: Why is rng = random.Random(42); rng.shuffle(idx) strictly safer inside a notebook than random.seed(42); random.shuffle(idx)?
Zero Test-Ratio Slice Trap: Suppose indices has length 10 and n_test = int(10 * 0.0) == 0. What does indices[-n_test:] evaluate to in Python, and why does indices[:n_test] avoid this bug?
Git Diff Bloat: Why do research teams strip cell "outputs" before committing .ipynb files to Git?

13.7.1 Exam Task 13.1 (30 Points): Audit Notebook Reproducibility
Write audit_notebook_reproducibility(nb_path) to inspect any .ipynb file on disk:

Load nb_path as UTF-8 JSON and count "code" cells ("code_cells") and "markdown" cells ("markdown_cells").
Compute "out_of_order" (True if any code cell has execution_count is None or <= previous executed count, else False).
Compute "has_outputs" (True if any code cell has non-empty "outputs", else False) and "clean_for_git" (not has_outputs).
Return the 5-key dictionary {"code_cells": int, "markdown_cells": int, "out_of_order": bool, "has_outputs": bool, "clean_for_git": bool}.



13.7.2 Exam Task 13.2 (35 Points): Extract Code Cells to Pure Python Module
Write extract_code_to_module(nb_path, py_out_path) to graduate a prototype notebook into a clean importable .py module:

Load nb_path as UTF-8 JSON and extract only "code" cells (ignoring markdown cells).
Skip every line whose stripped text starts with ! or % (shell escapes and line/cell magics).
Join non-empty code cell blocks with blank lines ("\n\n"), write the UTF-8 .py file to py_out_path, and return the integer count of non-empty code lines written.



13.7.3 Exam Task 13.3 (35 Points): Resume or Atomically Initialize Experiment
Write resume_or_init_experiment(ckpt_path, default_state) for disconnect-proof Colab experiments:

If ckpt_path exists and parses cleanly as a JSON dict, load and return (loaded_state, True).
Otherwise (missing file, corrupted/truncated JSON raising json.JSONDecodeError, or valid non-dict JSON such as a list), deep-copy default_state, atomically write it to ckpt_path via .tmp + .replace(), and return (copy_of_default, False).

text:
13.8 Stage 8 — Complete Annotated Solutions & Debugging Post-Mortem

13.8.1 A. Concept & Execution Trace Test Key

Because cell 2 ran at count 4 after cell 3 ran at count 2, cell 3’s output was computed from stale kernel state—running Restart & Run All may produce completely different results or crash.
It returns True, because an unexecuted code cell (execution_count is None) has never been verified during a clean top-to-bottom run.
.copy() creates a shallow copy whose "cells" list still points to the exact same inner cell dictionaries in memory; mutating cell["outputs"] = [] modifies the caller’s original nb_dict. copy.deepcopy(nb_dict) copies all nested lists and dicts safely.
It was permanently deleted when Google Colab recycled the ephemeral VM. Persistent outputs must be written to mounted Google Drive or exported to Git/cloud storage.
Colab enforces rolling GPU usage quotas; burning GPU hours on CPU-bound data cleaning can lock you out of GPU access when you actually need to train a deep-learning model later.
SyntaxError, because ! shell escapes and % magics are IPython preprocessor directives, not valid Python grammar.
train_state.json still contains the intact epoch-10 checkpoint, because the crash occurred while writing to train_state.tmp before tmp_path.replace(target) ever ran.
random.Random(seed) isolates its internal PRNG state inside a local object so unrelated random calls in other notebook cells can never perturb your train/test split.
In Python, -0 == 0, so indices[-0:] is identical to indices[0:] and wrongly returns all 10 elements! Using indices[:n_test] returns [] cleanly when n_test == 0.
Embedded outputs (especially base64-encoded matplotlib PNGs and noisy execution counts) bloat repository size and generate unreadable multi-thousand-line merge conflicts on every edit.



13.8.2 B. Annotated Solutions — Guided To-Dos (Mirrored in 02_guided_todos_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random

# To-Do 13.1
def detect_out_of_order_cells(nb_dict):
    """Return True if any code cell is unexecuted or out of order."""
    prev = 0
    for cell in nb_dict.get("cells", []):
        if cell.get("cell_type") != "code":
            continue
        ec = cell.get("execution_count")
        if ec is None or ec <= prev:
            return True
        prev = ec
    return False

# To-Do 13.2
def strip_notebook_outputs(nb_dict):
    """Return a deep copy of nb_dict with cleared code cell outputs."""
    cleaned = copy.deepcopy(nb_dict)
    for cell in cleaned.get("cells", []):
        if cell.get("cell_type") == "code":
            cell["outputs"] = []
            cell["execution_count"] = None
    return cleaned

# To-Do 13.3
def build_colab_url(owner, repo, branch, rel_path):
    """Return the Google Colab GitHub launch URL for rel_path."""
    clean_path = str(rel_path).lstrip("/")
    return (
        "https://colab.research.google.com/github/"
        f"{owner}/{repo}/blob/{branch}/{clean_path}"
    )

# To-Do 13.4
def resolve_data_path(filename, drive_dir=None, local_dir=None):
    """Resolve filename from drive_dir first, then local_dir."""
    for directory in (drive_dir, local_dir):
        if directory is not None:
            candidate = Path(directory) / filename
            if candidate.exists():
                return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Dataset not found: {filename}")

# To-Do 13.5
def save_checkpoint_atomic(ckpt_path, state_dict):
    """Atomically write state_dict as UTF-8 JSON via a .tmp file."""
    target = Path(ckpt_path)
    tmp_path = target.with_suffix(".tmp")
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(state_dict, f, indent=2)
    tmp_path.replace(target)

# To-Do 13.6
def seeded_train_test_indices(n_samples, test_ratio=0.2, seed=42):
    """Return deterministic (train_idx, test_idx) via local RNG."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    indices = list(range(n_samples))
    rng.shuffle(indices)
    n_test = int(n_samples * test_ratio)
    return indices[n_test:], indices[:n_test]


13.8.3 C. Annotated Solutions — Chapter 13 Coding Exam (Mirrored in 03_coding_exam_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

# Exam Task 13.1 (30 pts)
def audit_notebook_reproducibility(nb_path):
    """Audit .ipynb cell counts, execution order, and Git cleanliness."""
    with open(nb_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        nb = json.load(f)

    code_cells = 0
    markdown_cells = 0
    out_of_order = False
    has_outputs = False
    prev = 0

    for cell in nb.get("cells", []):
        ctype = cell.get("cell_type")
        if ctype == "markdown":
            markdown_cells += 1
        elif ctype == "code":
            code_cells += 1
            ec = cell.get("execution_count")
            if ec is None or ec <= prev:
                out_of_order = True
            else:
                prev = ec
            if cell.get("outputs"):
                has_outputs = True

    return {
        "code_cells": code_cells,
        "markdown_cells": markdown_cells,
        "out_of_order": out_of_order,
        "has_outputs": has_outputs,
        "clean_for_git": not has_outputs,
    }

# Exam Task 13.2 (35 pts)
def extract_code_to_module(nb_path, py_out_path):
    """Export code cells without !/% magics to .py and return line count."""
    with open(nb_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        nb = json.load(f)

    blocks = []
    for cell in nb.get("cells", []):
        if cell.get("cell_type") != "code":
            continue
        src = cell.get("source", [])
        text = "".join(src) if isinstance(src, list) else src
        kept = [
            line for line in text.splitlines()
            if not line.lstrip().startswith(("!", "%"))
        ]
        block = "\n".join(kept).strip("\n")
        if block:
            blocks.append(block)

    content = ("\n\n".join(blocks) + "\n") if blocks else ""
    with open(py_out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out_f:
        out_f.write(content)
    return sum(1 for line in content.splitlines() if line.strip())

# Exam Task 13.3 (35 pts)
def resume_or_init_experiment(ckpt_path, default_state):
    """Resume valid JSON dict checkpoint or atomically initialize it."""
    target = Path(ckpt_path)
    if target.exists():
        try:
            with open(target, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                loaded = json.load(f)
            if isinstance(loaded, dict):
                return loaded, True
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
            pass

    fresh = copy.deepcopy(default_state)
    tmp_path = target.with_suffix(".tmp")
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out_f:
        json.dump(fresh, out_f, indent=2)
    tmp_path.replace(target)
    return fresh, False


13.8.4 D. Debugging Post-Mortem: Top 3 Chapter 13 Failure Modes

Mutating Input Notebooks via Shallow Copy or Touching Markdown Cells: Calling nb_dict.copy() leaves the nested "cells" list shared with the caller, silently wiping original outputs in place; similarly, accessing cell["execution_count"] without checking cell.get("cell_type") == "code" crashes on the very first markdown heading.
Corrupting Checkpoints on Mid-Write Disconnects: Writing JSON straight to ckpt_path truncates the previous good state the instant open(..., "w") executes. Always stage writes in target.with_suffix(".tmp"), swap with tmp_path.replace(target), and catch json.JSONDecodeError during resume.
Leaving Magics in Exported .py Files or Sharing Global RNG State: Failing to filter ! and % lines produces broken .py modules that raise SyntaxError on import, while relying on global random.seed() lets an interactive exploration cell silently alter your held-out test indices.








NoteNotebook & Colab Engineering Unlocked!



Your notebooks are now auditable, Git-clean, crash-resilient, and deterministically reproducible across both Google Colab and local machines. In the next chapter, we scale these engineering habits to full scientific repositories with Git version control, virtual environments, and automated testing.

Learning Objectives
By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

Configure VS Code with a project-specific Python interpreter and inspect live program state with breakpoints, step-over controls, and the Variables/Call Stack panels.
Create isolated project environments with python -m venv .venv or uv venv, explain why exact version pins (==) prevent silent numerical drift, and parse or audit requirements.txt files programmatically.
Refactor exploratory Jupyter notebook cells into reusable .py modules protected by if __name__ == "__main__": entry guards.
Structure and validate a modern src/-layout Python package (pyproject.toml, src/<pkg>/__init__.py, tests/) and normalize messy project titles into valid snake_case Python import names.
Separate local API keys and database URLs from source code using gitignored .env files parsed safely with split("=", 1).
Build testable command-line tools using argparse.ArgumentParser and explicit parse_args(argv) lists, and diagnose ModuleNotFoundError, SystemExit, and malformed .env ValueError failures.

section: 14.1 Stage 1 — First-Principles Intuition: Escaping the Single-Notebook Cliff
text:
14.1 Stage 1 — First-Principles Intuition: Escaping the Single-Notebook Cliff
Jupyter notebooks and Google Colab are unmatched for exploration: loading a fresh maternal-health CSV, plotting hemoglobin histograms, and checking edge cases interactively. Yet every growing research project eventually hits the Single-Notebook Cliff:

Cell 47 silently depends on a variable you mutated back in Cell 12 and forgot to re-run.
Copy-pasting your triage helper across three manuscript notebooks creates three slightly incompatible versions of the same clinical cutoff.
Six months later, upgrading pandas globally for a new project breaks your published paper’s analysis script—the dreaded “it worked on my laptop last semester” failure.

Professional research software engineering solves all three problems by separating exploration (thin notebooks) from reusable logic (importable .py modules inside a src/ package), execution (typed argparse CLIs), and isolation (one virtual environment per project).






NoteMental Model — The Sterile Clinical Laboratory Bench



Think of a professional Python project like a biosafety-certified wet lab:

Sealed Reagent Cabinet (.venv / uv): Every study gets its own private shelf of exact reagent concentrations (pandas==2.2.0, numpy==1.26.4). Updating a package in Project B can never contaminate Project A.
Standard Operating Procedures (src/<pkg>/): Validated helper functions live in clean .py modules with unit tests (tests/), while notebooks stay short and import directly from your package (from mch_tools import classify_hb).
Lab Instrument Dial (argparse CLI): Instead of editing hardcoded filenames inside a script before every batch run, you pass typed flags (--input dhaka.csv --threshold 11.0) from the terminal—creating an auditable command history.
Locked Safe (.env): Private tokens, clinic server credentials, and local paths stay in a gitignored .env file, never committed into public GitHub repositories.
Microscope Under Glass (VS Code Debugger): Rather than scattering temporary print() statements everywhere, VS Code breakpoints pause execution mid-flight so you can inspect every local variable and step line-by-line.

    end

 Chapter 14 visual mental model: Notebook-to-Package & Environment Isolation 



Notice why the src/ layout is recommended by the Python Packaging Authority (PyPA):

No Accidental Local Imports: If your package lives directly in the repository root (./mch_tools/), Python can import the uninstalled local folder by mistake and hide packaging bugs. Placing code inside src/mch_tools/ forces you to install the package properly (pip install -e . or uv pip install -e .) inside .venv—guaranteeing your tests verify the exact package your collaborators will install.
Exact Reproducibility Boundary: A project’s pyproject.toml declares its build metadata and broad compatibility, while a pinned lockfile (requirements.txt with == or uv.lock) freezes every exact package version for manuscript replication.

section: 14.3 Stage 3 — Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough & Error Anatomy
text:
14.3 Stage 3 — Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough & Error Anatomy
Open part_03_engineering_workflow/ch14_vscode_packages/01_walkthrough.ipynb in Colab and run every cell alongside the dissections below.

14.3.1 Working Professionally in VS Code: Interpreters & Breakpoints
When you open your project folder locally in Visual Studio Code, follow this three-step engineering checklist before writing a single line:

Select the Virtual Environment Interpreter: Press Ctrl+Shift+P (macOS: Cmd+Shift+P), run Python: Select Interpreter, and pick .venv/bin/python (Windows: .venv\Scripts\python.exe). Check the bottom-right status bar to confirm VS Code is bound to your project’s .venv, not the global system Python.
Use Breakpoints Instead of print() Spam: Click the left gutter next to any line number to place a red breakpoint dot, then press F5 (Python Debugger: Current File). Execution pauses before that line runs so you can inspect every local variable in the Variables pane, evaluate expressions in the Debug Console, and step through code with Step Over (F10) or Step Into (F11).
Create & Activate .venv from the Integrated Terminal (`Ctrl+``):

# Built-in standard-library venv (works everywhere)
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e .

# Ultra-fast modern alternative with uv
uv venv .venv
uv pip install -e .






TipWhy pip install -e . (Editable Install) Changes Everything



Passing -e (“editable mode”) links your src/<pkg>/ folder directly into .venv/lib/.../site-packages. Any edit you save in VS Code takes effect immediately in every notebook, CLI command, and pytest run—without ever re-running pip install or hacking sys.path.





14.3.2 Notebook-to-Module Refactoring & if __name__ == "__main__":
When you extract a tested function out of a notebook into a .py file, wrap any demo or CLI execution inside if __name__ == "__main__":. Python sets __name__ to "__main__" only when the file is executed directly (python triage_utils.py), and to the module’s own name ("triage_utils") whenever another file imports it:
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

module_code = '''
def classify_hb(hb_g_dl, cutoff=11.0):
    """Return 'Anemic' if hb_g_dl < cutoff else 'Normal'."""
    return "Anemic" if hb_g_dl < cutoff else "Normal"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("CLI smoke test:", classify_hb(10.2))
'''

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    mod_path = Path(tmp) / "triage_utils.py"
    mod_path.write_text(module_code.strip() + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "triage_utils", mod_path
    )
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

    print("Imported __name__:", mod.__name__)
    print("Hb 10.4 ->", mod.classify_hb(10.4))
    print("Hb 12.1 ->", mod.classify_hb(12.1))
Expected Output:
Imported __name__: triage_utils
Hb 10.4 -> Anemic
Hb 12.1 -> Normal
Notice that "CLI smoke test: Anemic" did not print on import! Because mod.__name__ evaluated to "triage_utils", the if __name__ == "__main__": guard kept the import completely side-effect-free.



14.3.3 Virtual Environments, sys.prefix, & Dependency Files
Python itself knows whether it is running inside an isolated virtual environment by comparing sys.prefix against sys.base_prefix. Meanwhile, auditing requirements.txt lets you verify whether every dependency is pinned with == rather than loose ranges (>=, <=, ~=) or bare names:
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile

in_venv = sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix
print("Python version:", sys.version.split()[0])
print("Inside virtual env:", in_venv)

req_text = (
    "# Pinned cohort pipeline dependencies\n"
    "pandas==2.2.0\n"
    "numpy>=1.26\n"
    "scipy\n"
)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    req_path = Path(tmp) / "requirements.txt"
    req_path.write_text(req_text, encoding="utf-8")
    reqs = {}
    with open(req_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for raw in f:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            for op in ("==", ">=", "<=", "~="):
                if op in line:
                    pkg, ver = line.split(op, 1)
                    reqs[pkg.strip().lower()] = op + ver.strip()
                    break
            else:
                reqs[line.lower()] = ""
    print("Parsed requirements:", reqs)
Expected Output (version and venv status depend on your runtime):
Python version: 3.12.x
Inside virtual env: True
Parsed requirements: {'pandas': '==2.2.0', 'numpy': '>=1.26', 'scipy': ''}
Key mechanics in the parser loop:

Operator preservation (op + ver.strip()): Calling line.split(op, 1) consumes op, so concatenating op back keeps "==2.2.0" distinct from ">=2.2.0".
for ... else: idiom: Python runs the else: block only if the for op loop finishes without hitting break—catching bare package names like "scipy" cleanly.




14.3.4 Standard src/ Package Layout & .env Configuration
A minimal, production-ready scientific package contains pyproject.toml, src/<pkg>/__init__.py, and tests/, while keeping local tokens in a gitignored .env file:
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)
    (root / "src" / "mch_tools").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "tests").mkdir()
    (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        '[project]\nname = "mch_tools"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (root / "src" / "mch_tools" / "__init__.py").write_text(
        '__version__ = "0.1.0"\n', encoding="utf-8"
    )
    env_path = root / ".env"
    env_path.write_text(
        '# Local secrets (never commit to Git!)\n'
        'STUDY_ID="MCH-BD-2026"\n'
        "API_TOKEN='demo-key-99'\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    has_pyp = (root / "pyproject.toml").is_file()
    has_init = (root / "src" / "mch_tools" / "__init__.py").is_file()
    has_tests = (root / "tests").is_dir()
    print("Layout valid:", has_pyp and has_init and has_tests)

    env_vars = {}
    for raw in env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        key, val = line.split("=", 1)
        val = val.strip()
        if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1] and val[0] in ('"', "'"):
            val = val[1:-1]
        env_vars[key.strip()] = val
    print("Loaded .env keys:", env_vars)
Expected Output:
Layout valid: True
Loaded .env keys: {'STUDY_ID': 'MCH-BD-2026', 'API_TOKEN': 'demo-key-99'}






WarningWhy split('=', 1) Beats split('=') for .env Files



API tokens, base64 keys, and query URLs frequently contain = characters inside the value (for example, QUERY_URL="https://api.clinic.org/v1?site=dhaka"). Passing maxsplit=1 via line.split("=", 1) splits only on the first =, keeping the value completely intact.





14.3.5 Reproducible CLI Tools with argparse.parse_args([...])
Python’s standard-library argparse module validates required flags, converts strings directly to float or int, handles boolean switches (action="store_true"), and generates --help documentation automatically. Passing an explicit list into parser.parse_args([...]) lets you test your CLI inside notebooks and pytest without touching sys.argv:
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
    description="Screen a cohort CSV for maternal anemia."
)
parser.add_argument("--input", type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=11.0)
parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")

args = parser.parse_args(
    ["--input", "dhaka_mch.csv", "--threshold", "10.5", "--verbose"]
)
print("Input file:", args.input)
print("Cutoff (g/dL):", args.threshold, type(args.threshold).__name__)
print("Verbose mode:", args.verbose)
Expected Output:
Input file: dhaka_mch.csv
Cutoff (g/dL): 10.5 float
Verbose mode: True



14.3.6 Break It On Purpose! (Packaging, CLI & .env Error Anatomy)






ImportantBreak It On Purpose #1 — ModuleNotFoundError on Uninstalled Package



# Intentional Bug #1: ModuleNotFoundError — missing or uninstalled pkg
import nonexistent_clinic_pkg
Python’s Traceback:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nonexistent_clinic_pkg'
Diagnosis: Python searched every directory in sys.path (standard library + active .venv/site-packages) and found no package with that name. In real projects, this almost always means either you forgot to activate .venv in VS Code or you haven’t run pip install -e . yet.
Fix: Select the .venv interpreter in VS Code, run pip install -e ., and confirm your import name uses underscores (_), not hyphens (-).








ImportantBreak It On Purpose #2 — SystemExit from Missing Required argparse Flag



# Intentional Bug #2: SystemExit — missing required --input CLI flag
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="screen_cohort")
parser.add_argument("--input", type=str, required=True)
parser.parse_args([])
Python’s Traceback:
usage: screen_cohort [-h] --input INPUT
screen_cohort: error: the following arguments are required: --input
SystemExit: 2
Diagnosis: When a required flag is omitted (or a --threshold receives non-numeric text), argparse prints a usage hint to stderr and raises SystemExit(2) to halt the script cleanly with a non-zero exit code.
Fix: Supply every required flag (["--input", "cohort.csv"]), and remember to pass an explicit argv list when testing CLI parsers inside Jupyter or Colab!








ImportantBreak It On Purpose #3 — ValueError Unpacking Malformed .env Line



# Intentional Bug #3: ValueError — malformed .env line missing '='
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    bad_env = Path(tmp) / ".env"
    bad_env.write_text("API_TOKEN_WITHOUT_EQUALS\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for raw in bad_env.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        key, value = raw.split("=", 1)
Python’s Traceback:
ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)
Diagnosis: raw.split("=", 1) returned a 1-element list because the line lacked =, so tuple unpacking into key, value raised ValueError.
Fix: Always skip empty lines and # comments first, and validate "=" in line (or raise a clear diagnostic error with the offending line number) before unpacking.

14.4 Stage 4 — The Researcher’s Problem-Structuring Blueprint
Scenario: Before submitting supplementary code to a peer-reviewed journal, your lab runs an automated pre-submission gatekeeper. Write check_package_readiness(root_dir, raw_pkg_name, req_path) that normalizes a messy repository name (like "Dhaka-Epi"), verifies the three required src/ layout artifacts (pyproject.toml, src/<pkg>/__init__.py, tests/), scans requirements.txt for any dependency missing an exact == pin, and returns a structured readiness report dictionary.

14.4.1 Blueprint (Completed on Paper Before Coding)

Input & Output Contract:

Inputs: root_dir (Path or str), raw_pkg_name (str), req_path (Path or str).
Output: {"package": str, "layout_ok": bool, "unpinned": list[str], "ready": bool}.

Edge Cases & Traps:

Normalize raw_pkg_name (strip, lowercase, replace - and spaces with _, collapse repeated _, strip outer _) before constructing root / "src" / pkg / "__init__.py".
Ignore blank lines and # comments in requirements.txt.
Sort unpinned alphabetically for deterministic reports.

Step-by-Step Algorithm:

Normalize raw_pkg_name into pkg.
Check .is_file() for pyproject.toml and src/<pkg>/__init__.py, and .is_dir() for tests.
Read req_path; for each non-comment line lacking "==", split off any version operator (>, <, ~, =) and collect the lowercased package name.
Sort unpinned, set ready = layout_ok and len(unpinned) == 0, and return the report dict.

Verification Plan (Hand Check):

For "Dhaka-Epi" with valid src/dhaka_epi/__init__.py and requirements.txt containing pandas==2.2.0 + numpy>=1.26: package="dhaka_epi", layout_ok=True, unpinned=["numpy"], ready=False.




14.4.2 Clean Python Implementation (Verbatim in 01_walkthrough.ipynb)
from pathlib import Path
import re
import tempfile

def check_package_readiness(root_dir, raw_pkg_name, req_path):
    """Normalize name, check src/ layout, and flag unpinned deps."""
    cleaned = raw_pkg_name.strip().lower()
    cleaned = cleaned.replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    pkg = re.sub(r"_+", "_", cleaned).strip("_")

    root = Path(root_dir)
    layout_ok = (
        (root / "pyproject.toml").is_file()
        and (root / "src" / pkg / "__init__.py").is_file()
        and (root / "tests").is_dir()
    )

    unpinned = []
    for raw in Path(req_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if "==" not in line:
            name = re.split(r"[><~=]", line, maxsplit=1)[0]
            unpinned.append(name.strip().lower())

    unpinned.sort()
    return {
        "package": pkg,
        "layout_ok": layout_ok,
        "unpinned": unpinned,
        "ready": layout_ok and len(unpinned) == 0,
    }

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    proj = Path(tmp)
    (proj / "src" / "dhaka_epi").mkdir(parents=True)
    (proj / "tests").mkdir()
    (proj / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        '[project]\nname = "dhaka_epi"\n', encoding="utf-8"
    )
    (proj / "src" / "dhaka_epi" / "__init__.py").write_text(
        '__version__ = "0.1.0"\n', encoding="utf-8"
    )
    req = proj / "requirements.txt"
    req.write_text("pandas==2.2.0\nnumpy>=1.26\n", encoding="utf-8")
    report = check_package_readiness(proj, "Dhaka-Epi", req)
    print("Readiness audit:", report)
Output:
Readiness audit: {'package': 'dhaka_epi', 'layout_ok': True,
'unpinned': ['numpy'], 'ready': False}

14.6 Stage 6 — Concept & Execution Trace Test (No Computer Allowed!)
Test your understanding on paper before consulting Stage 8:

Module Entry Guard: A file metrics.py contains print("Loading...") at top level and print("Running CLI...") inside if __name__ == "__main__":. What prints when another script runs import metrics?
Virtual Environment Detection: How does Python distinguish whether it is running inside a .venv versus the global system interpreter using the sys module?
Why Pin with ==? Why can numpy>=1.26 in a manuscript’s requirements.txt fail reproducibility two years later, whereas numpy==1.26.4 locks the environment?
Editable Install (-e): After running pip install -e . on a src/-layout package, do you need to re-run pip install every time you edit a function in src/mch_tools/stats.py?
Why src/ Beats Flat Layout: What subtle testing bug does placing your package inside src/<pkg>/ prevent compared to placing <pkg>/ directly in the repository root?
Notebook argparse Crash: Why does calling parser.parse_args() with no arguments inside a Jupyter or Colab cell crash with SystemExit: 2? How do you make it testable?
action="store_true" Default: In parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true"), what value does args.verbose hold when --verbose is omitted from argv?
PyPI vs. Python Identifier: Why is sharukh-tutor valid in pip install sharukh-tutor and pyproject.toml, yet import sharukh-tutor raises SyntaxError?
.env Splitting Trap: Given the .env line DB_URL="postgres://host/db?sslmode=require", what happens if you parse it with key, val = line.split("=") instead of line.split("=", 1)?
VS Code Breakpoint Advantage: During debugging in VS Code, what is the difference between Step Over (F10) and Step Into (F11) when paused on a function call like clean_vitals(row)?

text:
14.8 Stage 8 — Complete Annotated Solutions & Debugging Post-Mortem

14.8.1 A. Concept & Execution Trace Test Key

Only Loading... prints. During import metrics, Python sets __name__ == "metrics", so the if __name__ == "__main__": block is skipped.
Compare sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix. Inside an active virtual environment, sys.prefix points to .venv while sys.base_prefix points to the base Python installation.
numpy>=1.26 allows future major releases (such as 2.x) with breaking API or floating-point changes; numpy==1.26.4 pins the exact release used for your paper.
No. Editable mode (-e) links .venv directly to your live src/ directory, so saved code edits are reflected immediately on the next import or test run.
In a flat layout, Python can import the uninstalled local directory directly, masking missing files or broken pyproject.toml metadata that would fail for external users. The src/ layout forces tests to import the installed package.
Without arguments, parser.parse_args() inspects sys.argv[1:], which contains Jupyter’s internal kernel flags (like -f kernel.json) that your parser doesn’t recognize. Pass an explicit list parser.parse_args(argv) instead.
False (action="store_true" defaults to False when omitted and switches to True when present).
Python parses - as the subtraction operator in import statements, so importable package directories must use underscores (sharukh_tutor).
line.split("=") produces 3 parts ("DB_URL", '"postgres://host/db?sslmode', 'require"'), raising ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2). Using line.split("=", 1) splits only once.
Step Over (F10) executes clean_vitals(row) as a single step and pauses on the next line of the caller; Step Into (F11) jumps inside the body of clean_vitals so you can trace it line by line.



14.8.2 B. Annotated Solutions — Guided To-Dos (Mirrored in 02_guided_todos_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import re

# To-Do 14.1
def parse_requirements_file(req_path):
    """Parse requirements.txt into dict of pkg_lower -> spec_or_empty."""
    reqs = {}
    with open(req_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for raw in f:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            for op in ("==", ">=", "<=", "~="):
                if op in line:
                    name, version = line.split(op, 1)
                    reqs[name.strip().lower()] = op + version.strip()
                    break
            else:
                reqs[line.lower()] = ""
    return reqs

# To-Do 14.2
def find_unpinned_packages(req_dict):
    """Return sorted list of package names not pinned with '=='."""
    return sorted(
        pkg for pkg, spec in req_dict.items()
        if not spec.startswith("==")
    )

# To-Do 14.3
def build_cli_parser():
    """Return an ArgumentParser with --input, --threshold, --verbose."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Clinical cohort analysis CLI"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--input", type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=11.0)
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    return parser

# To-Do 14.4
def validate_src_package_layout(root_dir, pkg_name):
    """Check pyproject.toml, src/<pkg>/__init__.py, and tests/ dir."""
    root = Path(root_dir)
    has_pyproject = (root / "pyproject.toml").is_file()
    has_init = (root / "src" / pkg_name / "__init__.py").is_file()
    has_tests = (root / "tests").is_dir()
    return {
        "has_pyproject": has_pyproject,
        "has_init": has_init,
        "has_tests": has_tests,
        "is_valid": has_pyproject and has_init and has_tests,
    }

# To-Do 14.5
def normalize_package_name(raw_name):
    """Normalize raw project name into snake_case package name."""
    cleaned = raw_name.strip().lower()
    cleaned = cleaned.replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    cleaned = re.sub(r"_+", "_", cleaned)
    return cleaned.strip("_")

# To-Do 14.6
def load_env_file(env_path):
    """Parse KEY=VALUE pairs from .env ignoring comments and blanks."""
    env = {}
    with open(env_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for raw in f:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            key, val = line.split("=", 1)
            key, val = key.strip(), val.strip()
            if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1]:
                if val[0] in ('"', "'"):
                    val = val[1:-1]
            env[key] = val
    return env


14.8.3 C. Annotated Solutions — Chapter 14 Coding Exam (Mirrored in 03_coding_exam_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import re

# Exam Task 14.1 (30 pts)
def audit_dependencies(req_path):
    """Audit requirements.txt and return reproducibility report."""
    reqs = {}
    with open(req_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for raw in f:
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            for op in ("==", ">=", "<=", "~="):
                if op in line:
                    name, ver = line.split(op, 1)
                    reqs[name.strip().lower()] = op + ver.strip()
                    break
            else:
                reqs[line.lower()] = ""

    unpinned = sorted(
        pkg for pkg, spec in reqs.items()
        if not spec.startswith("==")
    )
    total = len(reqs)
    return {
        "total": total,
        "pinned_count": total - len(unpinned),
        "unpinned": unpinned,
        "reproducible": len(unpinned) == 0,
    }

# Exam Task 14.2 (35 pts)
def scaffold_research_package(base_dir, pkg_name):
    """Create a src-layout research package and return POSIX paths."""
    cleaned = pkg_name.strip().lower()
    cleaned = cleaned.replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    pkg = re.sub(r"_+", "_", cleaned).strip("_")

    root = Path(base_dir)
    files = {
        "pyproject.toml": (
            f'[project]\nname = "{pkg}"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n'
        ),
        "README.md": f"# {pkg}\n\nReproducible research package.\n",
        f"src/{pkg}/__init__.py": (
            f'"""Core module for {pkg}."""\n__version__ = "0.1.0"\n'
        ),
        "tests/test_smoke.py": (
            f"import {pkg}\n\n"
            f"def test_version():\n"
            f"    assert hasattr({pkg}, '__version__')\n"
        ),
    }
    created = []
    for rel_path, content in files.items():
        target = root / rel_path
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
        created.append(target.relative_to(root).as_posix())
    return sorted(created)

# Exam Task 14.3 (35 pts)
def run_triage_cli(argv):
    """Parse clinical vitals from argv and return triage dict."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Clinical vitals triage CLI"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--temp", type=float, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--hb", type=float, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--sbp", type=int, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.temp >= 39.5 or args.sbp >= 170 or args.hb < 8.5:
        priority = "Urgent"
    elif args.temp >= 38.0 or args.sbp >= 140 or args.hb < 11.0:
        priority = "Moderate"
    else:
        priority = "Routine"

    return {
        "temp_c": args.temp,
        "hb_g_dl": args.hb,
        "sbp_mmhg": args.sbp,
        "priority": priority,
    }


14.8.4 D. Debugging Post-Mortem: Top 3 Chapter 14 Failure Modes

Wrong Interpreter Selected in VS Code (ModuleNotFoundError): Installing packages into .venv while VS Code’s terminal or notebook kernel still points to the global Python triggers immediate ModuleNotFoundError. Always check the bottom-right Python version badge in VS Code and confirm sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix.
Calling parser.parse_args() Without argv Inside Functions: Hardcoding parser.parse_args() inside library helpers reads sys.argv globally, breaking both Jupyter notebooks and pytest suites. Design CLI entrypoints around def main(argv=None): args = parser.parse_args(argv) so tests pass explicit lists cleanly.
Leaking .env Files or Leaving Unpinned Dependencies: Committing .env exposes credentials permanently in Git history, while leaving pandas or numpy>=1.26 unpinned invites silent breaking upgrades. Pair .gitignore (with .env and .venv/) with pinned lockfiles and an automated audit_dependencies() check before every release.








NoteEngineering Foundations Locked In!



You now have the exact project architecture used by professional scientific software teams: isolated .venv environments, src/-layout packages, breakpoint debugging in VS Code, secret-safe .env configs, and testable argparse CLIs. Next, we put these clean packages under automated version control with Git, GitHub, and pytest.

15.1 Stage 1 — First-Principles Intuition: Why analysis_FINAL_v3_fixed.py Fails Peer Review
Six months after submitting a manuscript, Reviewer #2 asks a routine question: “Table 2 reports a mean maternal hemoglobin of \(11.15\text{ g/dL}\) across \(N = 412\) mothers, yet your supplementary file has \(415\) rows—which three records were dropped, and which version of the cleaning script generated Figure 1?”
If your research folder contains clean_v1.py, clean_v2_new.py, and clean_FINAL_really.py alongside an unlogged overwrite of raw_data.csv, answering Reviewer #2 becomes a forensic nightmare. Professional scientific engineering eliminates this guesswork with four interlocking pillars:






NoteMental Model — The Audited Clinical Trial Lab Notebook



Think of a reproducible research repository like a regulated clinical trial binder:

Tamper-Evident History (Git & GitHub): Every edit is recorded as an immutable, cryptographically chained commit with a concise subject line, author, and timestamp—never overwritten by v2_final filenames.
Confidentiality Wall (.gitignore & Secret Scanners): Raw patient registries (*.csv) and credentials (.env, API tokens) stay strictly off GitHub while code, tests, and tiny provenance manifests are shared openly.
Typed, Self-Explaining Contracts (PEP 8, Ruff & Type Hints): Consistent formatting and explicit types (list[float], Optional[float], TypedDict) turn silent runtime surprises into immediate editor warnings.
Chain of Custody (logging & SHA-256 Fingerprints): Every pipeline run records its exact input file’s 64-character SHA-256 hash and logs every skipped sentinel row (INFO / WARNING) to disk.

15.2 Stage 2 — Visual Mental Model: Git’s 3-Zone & Remote Workflow
Before memorizing commands, lock in the four physical spaces where your research code lives and the exact commands that move snapshots between them:






flowchart TD
    subgraph Local["Local Machine"]
        direction LR
        W["1. Working Dir<br/>Edit scripts &<br/>notebooks"] -->|"git add"| S["2. Staging Area<br/>Next snapshot<br/>(Index)"]
        S -->|"git commit"| L["3. Local Repo<br/>Commit history<br/>(.git/ SHA-1)"]
    end
    subgraph Remote["Shared Origin"]
        direction LR
        R["4. GitHub Remote<br/>Shared origin, Pull Requests & Peer Review"]
    end
    Local -->|"git push"| Remote
    Remote -. "git pull" .-> Local


 Git three-zone local workflow and GitHub remote synchronization cycle 



Understanding those four zones explains almost every Git command you will ever run:

git add <file> copies selected changes from your Working Directory into the Staging Area, letting you bundle related edits into one atomic commit while leaving half-finished experiments unstaged.
git commit -m "..." seals the Staging Area into a permanent, content-addressed snapshot inside .git/ on your local machine—no internet connection required.
git switch -c feat/hb-audit creates an isolated feature branch so main always stays clean and paper-ready until your Pull Request passes review and pytest.
.gitignore + Pre-Commit Guard: Anything matching .gitignore never enters the Staging Area in the first place, keeping raw clinical files and .env secrets safely local.

text:
15.3 Stage 3 — Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough & Error Anatomy
Open part_03_engineering_workflow/ch15_git_clean_code/01_walkthrough.ipynb in Colab and execute every cell alongside the dissections below.

15.3.1 Everyday Git Workflow, .gitignore Auditing & Secret Scanning
In your local terminal (outside Colab), a clean feature-branch research cycle uses just seven core commands:
git status                               # Inspect working tree & stage
git switch -c feat/add-sha256-manifest   # Isolate new work on a branch
git add src/provenance.py tests/         # Stage only reviewed code
git diff --staged                        # Audit exact lines before commit
git commit -m "Add SHA-256 manifest builder for cohort CSVs"
git log --oneline -n 5                   # Verify concise commit history
git push -u origin feat/add-sha256-manifest
Notice the commit subject rule enforced by professional teams: keep the first line imperative, concise (\(5 \le \text{len} \le 72\) characters), and free of a trailing period so git log --oneline and GitHub Pull Request headers never truncate awkwardly.
Now let’s audit .gitignore coverage with Python’s standard-library fnmatch and scan a configuration snippet for leaked credentials—run this cell verbatim in 01_walkthrough.ipynb:
import fnmatch

gitignore_text = (
    "# Never commit raw clinical data or secrets\n"
    "*.csv\n"
    ".env\n"
    "*.log\n"
    "__pycache__/*\n"
)
staged_candidates = [
    "README.md",
    "src/clean_cohort.py",
    "raw_mch_2026.csv",
    ".env",
    "run.log",
]

patterns = [
    line.strip()
    for line in gitignore_text.splitlines()
    if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")
]
tracked = sorted(
    fname for fname in staged_candidates
    if not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(fname, pat) for pat in patterns)
)
print("Active .gitignore patterns:", patterns)
print("Safe to track in Git:", tracked)

config_sample = (
    "STUDY_ID = 'MCH-BD-2026'\n"
    "TOKEN = 'ghp_exampleLeak999'\n"
    "API_KEY=demo_secret_token\n"
)
secret_tags = ("ghp_", "AIza", "sk-", "API_KEY=", "PASSWORD=")
flagged_lines = [
    idx for idx, ln in enumerate(config_sample.splitlines(), start=1)
    if any(tag in ln for tag in secret_tags)
]
print("Flagged secret lines (1-based):", flagged_lines)
Expected Output:
Active .gitignore patterns: ['*.csv', '.env', '*.log', '__pycache__/*']
Safe to track in Git: ['README.md', 'src/clean_cohort.py']
Flagged secret lines (1-based): [2, 3]
Key mechanics to inspect closely:

Skipping Comments & Blank Lines: Lines starting with # are documentation inside .gitignore; failing to skip them would mistakenly treat # *.py as an ignore rule.
Negating any(...): not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(fname, pat) ...) returns the unignored files—the exact files Git is allowed to commit.
1-Based Line Numbers: enumerate(..., start=1) aligns flagged secret line numbers directly with VS Code, Vim, and GitHub diff line numbers.




15.3.2 Clean Code (PEP 8 / Ruff), Type Hints, and TypedDict Contracts
Clean research code follows PEP 8 conventions—snake_case function/variable names, PascalCase class names, UPPER_CASE constants, 4-space indentation, short readable lines, and one clear responsibility per function. Modern Python teams enforce these rules automatically in milliseconds with Ruff:
ruff check src/ tests/     # Flag unused imports, bugs & PEP 8 violations
ruff format src/ tests/    # Auto-format code to consistent style
Pairing Ruff with Python type hints (list[float], Optional[float], and TypedDict) documents the exact shape of every input and output without changing runtime speed:
from typing import Optional, TypedDict


class CohortSummary(TypedDict):
    site: str
    valid_n: int
    mean_hb: Optional[float]


def summarize_site_hb(
    site: str,
    readings: list[float],
) -> CohortSummary:
    """Return a typed hemoglobin summary for one clinic site."""
    clean = [val for val in readings if 3.0 <= val <= 22.0]
    mean_val: Optional[float] = (
        round(sum(clean) / len(clean), 2) if clean else None
    )
    return {
        "site": site.strip().title(),
        "valid_n": len(clean),
        "mean_hb": mean_val,
    }


dhaka_report = summarize_site_hb("  dhaka ", [10.4, 999.0, 11.6])
empty_report = summarize_site_hb("sylhet", [999.0])
print("Dhaka summary:", dhaka_report)
print("Empty summary:", empty_report)
Expected Output:
Dhaka summary: {'site': 'Dhaka', 'valid_n': 2, 'mean_hb': 11.0}
Empty summary: {'site': 'Sylhet', 'valid_n': 0, 'mean_hb': None}
Notice how Optional[float] explicitly warns every collaborator (and static type checkers like mypy or pyright) that mean_hb can be None when a cohort has zero valid rows—preventing downstream TypeError crashes before the pipeline ever runs.



15.3.3 Structured logging vs. print() (With Clean Handler Teardown)
print() is handy for quick interactive exploration, but it vanishes from terminal scrollback, has no severity levels (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL), and cannot be routed cleanly to an audit log file. Python’s standard-library logging module solves all three problems:
import logging
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    log_path = Path(tmp) / "cohort_run.log"
    logger = logging.getLogger("ch15_walkthrough_demo")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    logger.propagate = False

    handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
    fmt = logging.Formatter("[%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
    handler.setFormatter(fmt)
    logger.addHandler(handler)

    try:
        logger.info("Pipeline started for Dhaka ANC cohort")
        logger.warning("Row 4: skipped sentinel hb_g_dl='999'")
        logger.info("Pipeline completed: 2 valid, 1 skipped")
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()

    print(log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
Expected Output:
[INFO] Pipeline started for Dhaka ANC cohort
[WARNING] Row 4: skipped sentinel hb_g_dl='999'
[INFO] Pipeline completed: 2 valid, 1 skipped






WarningMandatory Logging Habit — Always Detach & Close FileHandlers!



Because logging.getLogger(name) returns the same singleton logger object across repeated function calls in a notebook or test suite, forgetting logger.removeHandler(handler) causes every future call to write duplicate lines, and forgetting handler.close() leaks open file handles that block tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() cleanup on Windows. Wrapping teardown in finally: guarantees spotless cleanup every single time.





15.3.4 Cryptographic Dataset Provenance (hashlib.sha256) & Research Templates
Because raw clinical CSV files stay out of Git (.gitignore), how do you prove six months later that data/raw/mch_v1.csv was never accidentally edited in Excel? You compute its SHA-256 cryptographic digest—a deterministic 64-character hexadecimal fingerprint where flipping even a single digit changes roughly half of the output bits (the avalanche effect):
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile


def sha256_file(filepath: Path) -> str:
    """Compute lowercase 64-char SHA-256 hex digest in 64 KB chunks."""
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(65536):
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    raw_csv = Path(tmp) / "mch_v1.csv"
    raw_csv.write_text("id,hb_g_dl\nP1,10.8\n", encoding="utf-8")
    digest_v1 = sha256_file(raw_csv)

    # Flip a single digit (10.8 -> 10.9) to demonstrate avalanche effect
    raw_csv.write_text("id,hb_g_dl\nP1,10.9\n", encoding="utf-8")
    digest_v2 = sha256_file(raw_csv)

    print("Digest v1 (first 16):", digest_v1[:16], "len=", len(digest_v1))
    print("Digest v2 (first 16):", digest_v2[:16], "len=", len(digest_v2))
    print("Identical files?:", digest_v1 == digest_v2)
Expected Output:
Digest v1 (first 16): b89b84008541b87d len= 64
Digest v2 (first 16): 8137e0963620b790 len= 64
Identical files?: False
Combine Git, .gitignore, type-checked src/ modules, tests/, and a tiny committed data/manifest.json inside a standardized Cookiecutter Data Science research project layout:
mch_anemia_study/
├── .gitignore              # Blocks data/raw/*.csv, .env, *.log, cache
├── README.md               # Study overview, setup & reproduction steps
├── pyproject.toml          # Dependencies, Ruff & pytest configuration
├── data/
│   ├── manifest.json       # Committed SHA-256 fingerprints (no PHI!)
│   ├── raw/                # Read-only source CSVs (gitignored)
│   └── processed/          # Regenerable clean cohorts (gitignored)
├── notebooks/              # Numbered exploratory notebooks (01_eda.ipynb)
├── src/
│   └── mch_study/          # Reusable, type-hinted Python modules
├── tests/                  # Automated pytest suite (Chapter 10)
└── reports/                # Figures & manuscript tables



15.3.5 Break It On Purpose! (Provenance & Logging Error Anatomy)






ImportantBreak It On Purpose #1 — FileNotFoundError Hashing a Missing Dataset



import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    missing_csv = Path(tmp) / "missing_cohort.csv"
    with open(missing_csv, "rb") as f:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
Python’s Traceback:
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'.../missing_cohort.csv'
Diagnosis: Calling open(path, "rb") or path.read_bytes() assumes the dataset exists on disk. In a provenance verifier, a deleted file should be reported cleanly as "missing" rather than crashing the audit script.
Fix: Guard with if not fpath.is_file(): before attempting to read bytes or compute a digest.








ImportantBreak It On Purpose #2 — TypeError Passing str Instead of bytes to hashlib.sha256



import hashlib

csv_text = "patient_id,hb_g_dl\nP01,11.2\n"
digest = hashlib.sha256(csv_text).hexdigest()
Python’s Traceback:
TypeError: Strings must be encoded before hashing
Diagnosis: Cryptographic hashes operate on raw bytes, never Unicode str objects (because the same characters can be encoded differently in UTF-8 vs. UTF-16). Passing a text string—or opening a file in text mode "r" instead of "rb"—immediately triggers TypeError.
Fix: Open files in binary mode ("rb") or call csv_text.encode("utf-8") before passing data into hashlib.sha256(...).








ImportantBreak It On Purpose #3 — ValueError on Invalid Logging Level String



import logging

bad_logger = logging.getLogger("ch15_bad_level_demo")
bad_logger.setLevel("URGENT")
Python’s Traceback:
ValueError: Unknown level: 'URGENT'
Diagnosis: Python’s logging module recognizes only the standard severity names ("DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL") or their integer constants. Passing a custom string like "URGENT" or a lowercase string like "info" directly to setLevel(...) raises ValueError.
Fix: Normalize input with .strip().upper() and validate it against the five standard level names before logging.

15.4 Stage 4 — The Researcher’s Problem-Structuring Blueprint
Scenario: Before tagging v1.0.0 on GitHub for manuscript submission, your PI wants a single automated gatekeeper function prepare_release_bundle(repo_dir, log_path) that: (1) hashes every .csv and .json file inside repo_dir / "data" into repo_dir / "manifest.json", (2) scans all .py scripts inside repo_dir / "src" for leaked secret prefixes, (3) writes an INFO/WARNING audit log to log_path with clean handler teardown, and (4) returns a typed ReleaseAudit dictionary indicating whether the bundle is release_ready.

15.4.1 Blueprint (Completed on Paper Before Coding)

Input & Output Contract:

Inputs: repo_dir: Path (containing data/ and src/) and log_path: Path.
Side effects: Indented manifest.json written inside repo_dir; audit log written cleanly to log_path.
Return value: ReleaseAudit (TypedDict) with data_files, manifest_path, secret_leaks, and release_ready.

Edge Cases & Traps:

Never leave the FileHandler attached or open—place logger.removeHandler(handler) and handler.close() inside finally:.
Sort data/ entries by filename so manifest.json diffs stay deterministic in Git.
Check p.is_file() before reading bytes so subdirectories never raise IsADirectoryError.

Step-by-Step Algorithm:

Configure an isolated logger (propagate = False) with a UTF-8 FileHandler.
Inside try:, hash all regular .csv/.json files in repo_dir / "data" into manifest.
Scan every *.py file in repo_dir / "src" line by line (1-based) for the five secret tokens; log a WARNING for every leak.
Write manifest.json with indent=2, compute ready = len(manifest) > 0 and leaks == 0, and log final status.
Detach and close the handler in finally:, then return the typed ReleaseAudit dict.

Verification Plan (Hand Check):

1 CSV file in data/ + 1 clean Python script in src/ \(\rightarrow\) data_files = 1, secret_leaks = 0, release_ready = True, and 2 INFO log lines.




15.4.2 Clean Python Implementation (Verbatim in 01_walkthrough.ipynb)
import hashlib
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from typing import TypedDict


class ReleaseAudit(TypedDict):
    data_files: int
    manifest_path: str
    secret_leaks: int
    release_ready: bool


def prepare_release_bundle(
    repo_dir: Path,
    log_path: Path,
) -> ReleaseAudit:
    """Build a SHA-256 manifest, scan src/ for secrets, and log audit."""
    logger = logging.getLogger("ch15_release_gate")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    logger.propagate = False
    handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("[%(levelname)s] %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(handler)

    secret_tags = ("ghp_", "AIza", "sk-", "API_KEY=", "PASSWORD=")
    manifest: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
    leaks = 0

    try:
        data_dir = repo_dir / "data"
        for p in sorted(data_dir.iterdir(), key=lambda x: x.name):
            if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in {".csv", ".json"}:
                digest = hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                manifest[p.name] = {
                    "bytes": p.stat().st_size,
                    "sha256": digest,
                }
        logger.info("Hashed %d dataset file(s)", len(manifest))

        src_dir = repo_dir / "src"
        for py_file in sorted(src_dir.glob("*.py")):
            text = py_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for ln_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
                if any(tag in line for tag in secret_tags):
                    leaks += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "Leak in %s line %d", py_file.name, ln_no
                    )

        manifest_file = repo_dir / "manifest.json"
        with open(manifest_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out_f:
            json.dump(manifest, out_f, indent=2)

        ready = len(manifest) > 0 and leaks == 0
        logger.info("Release ready: %s", ready)
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()

    return {
        "data_files": len(manifest),
        "manifest_path": manifest_file.name,
        "secret_leaks": leaks,
        "release_ready": ready,
    }


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    repo = Path(tmp)
    (repo / "data").mkdir()
    (repo / "src").mkdir()
    (repo / "data" / "mch_clean.csv").write_text(
        "id,hb_g_dl\nP1,11.4\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    (repo / "src" / "analyze.py").write_text(
        "STUDY = 'MCH-BD-2026'\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    audit_log = repo / "release_audit.log"
    result = prepare_release_bundle(repo, audit_log)
    print("Audit Result:\n" + json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print("Audit Log:\n" + audit_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
Output:
Audit Result:
{
  "data_files": 1,
  "manifest_path": "manifest.json",
  "secret_leaks": 0,
  "release_ready": true
}
Audit Log:
[INFO] Hashed 1 dataset file(s)
[INFO] Release ready: True

15.8 Stage 8 — Complete Annotated Solutions & Debugging Post-Mortem

15.8.1 A. Concept & Execution Trace Test Key

Only clean.py is recorded in the commit; the edits to notes.txt remain safely in the Working Directory (unstaged).
Feature branches keep main always clean, tested, and ready to reproduce published tables while you iterate safely—and let collaborators review changes via a Pull Request before merging.
Yes, analysis.py is returned as unignored because lines beginning with # are comments in .gitignore, not active ignore patterns.
True—commit subject validation checks only the first subject line, allowing longer explanatory paragraphs and punctuation in the commit body.
Real provider prefixes and environment variable keys (ghp_, AIza, sk-, API_KEY=, PASSWORD=) are case-sensitive; matching case-sensitively avoids false alarms on ordinary lowercase variable names or prose comments.
No—Python executes the function normally without raising TypeError because type hints are metadata checked by static tools (mypy, pyright, IDE linters), not enforced at runtime.
\(1 + 2 + 3 = 6\) total lines! Call 1 attaches handler #1 (1 line), call 2 attaches handler #2 (writes 2 lines), and call 3 attaches handler #3 (writes 3 lines). Always call logger.removeHandler(handler) and handler.close() in finally:.
open(path, "r").read() returns a decoded Unicode str, whereas hashlib.sha256() strictly requires raw bytes (from binary mode "rb").
Roughly half of all 64 hex characters change completely (producing a totally unrecognizable digest), so any silent spreadsheet edit, truncated download, or version mix-up is detected with near-certainty.
Raw .csv files may be huge or contain restricted patient/field data that must never be uploaded to public GitHub, whereas data/manifest.json is tiny, contains zero patient records, and cryptographically locks the exact dataset version required to reproduce the paper.



15.8.2 B. Annotated Solutions — Guided To-Dos (Mirrored in 02_guided_todos_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import fnmatch
import hashlib
import logging
from pathlib import Path

# To-Do 15.1
def check_gitignore_coverage(gitignore_text, filenames):
    """Return sorted list of filenames NOT matched by .gitignore."""
    patterns = [
        line.strip()
        for line in gitignore_text.splitlines()
        if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")
    ]
    unignored = [
        fname for fname in filenames
        if not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(fname, pat) for pat in patterns)
    ]
    return sorted(unignored)

# To-Do 15.2
def validate_commit_message(message):
    """Validate first commit subject line; return (is_valid, reason)."""
    lines = message.splitlines()
    subject = lines[0].strip() if lines else ""
    if not subject:
        return (False, "Subject line cannot be empty")
    if len(subject) < 5:
        return (False, "Subject line must be at least 5 characters")
    if len(subject) > 72:
        return (False, "Subject line must be at most 72 characters")
    if subject.endswith("."):
        return (False, "Subject line should not end with a period")
    return (True, "Valid commit subject")

# To-Do 15.3
def scan_for_leaked_secrets(text):
    """Return 1-based line numbers containing sensitive secret tokens."""
    patterns = ("ghp_", "AIza", "sk-", "API_KEY=", "PASSWORD=")
    return [
        line_no
        for line_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1)
        if any(pat in line for pat in patterns)
    ]

# To-Do 15.4
_LOG_LEVELS = {
    "DEBUG": logging.DEBUG,
    "INFO": logging.INFO,
    "WARNING": logging.WARNING,
    "ERROR": logging.ERROR,
    "CRITICAL": logging.CRITICAL,
}

def write_structured_log(log_path, level, message):
    """Append '[LEVEL] message' to log_path via a closed FileHandler."""
    level_name = level.strip().upper()
    if level_name not in _LOG_LEVELS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown log level: {level!r}")
    logger = logging.getLogger("ch15_todo_logger")
    logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
    logger.propagate = False
    handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="a", encoding="utf-8")
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("[%(levelname)s] %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    try:
        logger.log(_LOG_LEVELS[level_name], message)
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()

# To-Do 15.5
def compute_file_sha256(filepath):
    """Return lowercase 64-char SHA-256 hex digest of filepath."""
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(65536):
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()

# To-Do 15.6
def build_dataset_manifest(data_dir):
    """Map sorted .csv/.json filenames to byte size and SHA-256."""
    manifest = {}
    for p in sorted(Path(data_dir).iterdir(), key=lambda x: x.name):
        if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in {".csv", ".json"}:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            manifest[p.name] = {
                "bytes": p.stat().st_size,
                "sha256": digest,
            }
    return manifest


15.8.3 C. Annotated Solutions — Part III Capstone Coding Exam (Mirrored in 03_coding_exam_SOLUTION.ipynb)
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path

# Exam Task 15.1 (30 pts)
def audit_repo_hygiene(repo_dir):
    """Inspect repo_dir for docs, .gitignore, .env leaks & checkpoints."""
    root = Path(repo_dir)
    has_readme = (root / "README.md").is_file()
    has_gitignore = (root / ".gitignore").is_file()
    has_env_leak = (root / ".env").is_file()
    has_checkpoints = (root / ".ipynb_checkpoints").is_dir()
    ready_to_push = (
        has_readme
        and has_gitignore
        and not has_env_leak
        and not has_checkpoints
    )
    return {
        "has_readme": has_readme,
        "has_gitignore": has_gitignore,
        "has_env_leak": has_env_leak,
        "has_checkpoints": has_checkpoints,
        "ready_to_push": ready_to_push,
    }

# Exam Task 15.2 (35 pts)
def verify_data_provenance(data_dir, manifest_dict):
    """Verify data_dir files against manifest_dict SHA-256 digests."""
    root = Path(data_dir)
    matched = []
    modified = []
    missing = []
    for fname in sorted(manifest_dict):
        fpath = root / fname
        if not fpath.is_file():
            missing.append(fname)
            continue
        actual_sha = hashlib.sha256(fpath.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if actual_sha == manifest_dict[fname]["sha256"]:
            matched.append(fname)
        else:
            modified.append(fname)
    return {
        "matched": matched,
        "modified": modified,
        "missing": missing,
        "all_verified": len(modified) == 0 and len(missing) == 0,
    }

# Exam Task 15.3 (35 pts)
def run_logged_cleaning_pipeline(in_csv, out_json, log_path):
    """Hash, clean, log, and summarize hb_g_dl CSV to indented JSON."""
    src_sha = hashlib.sha256(Path(in_csv).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    logger = logging.getLogger("ch15_capstone_pipeline")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    logger.propagate = False
    handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("[%(levelname)s] %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(handler)

    valid_vals = []
    rejected = 0
    try:
        logger.info("Pipeline started (sha256=%s)", src_sha)
        with open(in_csv, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as in_f:
            for row_num, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader(in_f), start=1):
                raw = row["hb_g_dl"].strip()
                if raw in ("", "N/A", "999"):
                    rejected += 1
                    logger.warning("Row %d rejected: %r", row_num, raw)
                else:
                    valid_vals.append(float(raw))

        mean_hb = (
            round(sum(valid_vals) / len(valid_vals), 2)
            if valid_vals
            else None
        )
        summary = {
            "source_sha256": src_sha,
            "valid_count": len(valid_vals),
            "rejected_count": rejected,
            "mean_hb": mean_hb,
        }
        logger.info(
            "Pipeline finished: valid=%d, rejected=%d",
            len(valid_vals),
            rejected,
        )
    finally:
        logger.removeHandler(handler)
        handler.close()

    with open(out_json, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out_f:
        json.dump(summary, out_f, indent=2)
    return summary


15.8.4 D. Debugging Post-Mortem: Top 3 Chapter 15 Failure Modes

Leaking logging.FileHandler Across Calls: Adding a FileHandler to a named logger without logger.removeHandler(handler) and handler.close() inside a finally: block silently duplicates every subsequent log message and can lock tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() folders on cleanup.
Hashing Text Mode Instead of Binary Mode ("r" vs. "rb"): Passing decoded strings into hashlib.sha256() triggers TypeError: Strings must be encoded before hashing (or UnicodeDecodeError on binary assets). Always read raw bytes via open(path, "rb") or Path(path).read_bytes().
Forgetting Existence & Negation Guards: Returning matched files instead of unignored files in .gitignore audits, or hashing a missing manifest entry without checking fpath.is_file() first, flips security checks upside down or crashes mid-audit with FileNotFoundError.

text:
16.1 Stage 1 — First-Principles Intuition: Why Loops Collapse & Vectorization Wins
In Parts I–III, you built clean pure-Python algorithms, classes, and reproducible engineering workflows. Yet the moment a public health registry grows from 50 rows to 5,000,000 hospital records—or a neural network multiplies two \(1024 \times 1024\) weight matrices—a Python for loop hits a wall.
Why? Because a Python list is not a contiguous strip of numbers in RAM. Every element in a Python list is a separate heap-allocated PyObject box storing type tags, reference counts, and pointers. On every single iteration of for w, h in zip(weights, heights):, Python must chase pointers across memory, check data types dynamically, box a new float result, and repeat millions of times.
NumPy (ndarray) flips the architecture completely:

Homogeneous Contiguous Memory: All elements share a single fixed dtype (such as 64-bit float64, 8 bytes each) laid out back-to-back in one uninterrupted C memory block.
Vectorized C & BLAS Loops: Writing weights / ((heights / 100.0) ** 2) pushes the loop down into compiled C and CPU SIMD vector instructions, processing thousands of patients in microseconds.
Universal Scientific Substrate: Pandas DataFrames, Scikit-Learn feature matrices, SciPy solvers, and PyTorch/JAX tensors all inherit NumPy’s exact shape, axis, masking, and broadcasting semantics.







NoteMental Model — Warehouse Pallet vs. Scavenger Hunt



Think of a Python list as a scavenger hunt: the list only holds sticky notes pointing to scattered storage lockers across a warehouse, and you must unlock each locker and check its label before doing arithmetic. A NumPy ndarray is a shrink-wrapped warehouse pallet of identical 8-byte float bricks lined up in a straight row—a single forklift pass (CPU vector instruction) lifts and transforms the entire pallet at once.

16.2 Stage 2 — Visual Mental Model: Contiguous Memory, Axes & Broadcasting
Trace the three mental models that govern 95% of real-world NumPy code—contiguous RAM, 2D axis directions, and zero-copy broadcasting:






flowchart TD
    subgraph Mem["Contiguous RAM"]
        L["Python list: scattered PyObject pointers"]
        A["NumPy ndarray: packed C float64 block (8 B each)"]
    end
    subgraph Axes["2D Axes (3, 4)"]
        AX0["axis=0 (down rows): mean(X, axis=0) -> shape (4,)"]
        AX1["axis=1 (across cols): sum(X, axis=1) -> shape (3,)"]
    end
    subgraph Bcast["Broadcasting"]
        BC["(3, 4) - (4,) aligns trailing dims -> (3, 4)"]
    end
    A --> AX0
    A --> AX1
    AX0 -. "1D vector (4,)" .-> BC


 Chapter 16 visual mental model: Contiguous Memory, Axes & Broadcasting 



Keep one golden rule glued to your monitor whenever you pass axis=... on a 2D (rows, cols) matrix: the axis you specify is the axis that collapses (disappears)!

Collapsing axis=0 (rows) leaves one result per column: (3, 4) \(\rightarrow\) (4,).
Collapsing axis=1 (columns) leaves one result per row: (3, 4) \(\rightarrow\) (3,).







WarningThe View-vs-Copy Trap — Slicing a NumPy Array Does NOT Copy!



In pure Python (Chapter 7), sub = my_list[1:4] allocates a new list. In NumPy, sub = arr[1:4] returns a view pointing directly into arr’s original memory buffer! Mutating sub[0] = -1.0 silently overwrites arr[1]. Whenever you plan to clean, clip, or impute an input array inside a function, always start with np.array(x, dtype=float, copy=True) or x.copy().

16.3 Stage 3 — Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough & Error Anatomy
Open part_04_data_science_math/ch16_numpy_vectorization/01_walkthrough.ipynb in Colab and execute every cell alongside the dissections below.

16.3.1 Contiguous Arrays vs. Python Lists
import numpy as np

w_list = [64.5, 54.6, 70.0, 81.2]
h_list = [168.0, 156.0, 175.0, 180.0]

weights = np.array(w_list, dtype=float)
heights = np.array(h_list, dtype=float)

# List `* 2` repeats the container; NumPy `* 2` scales every value!
print("List * 2: ", w_list[:2] * 2)
print("Array * 2:", weights[:2] * 2)

# Vectorized BMI in one C-speed expression (zero Python for-loops)
bmi = np.round(weights / ((heights / 100.0) ** 2), 2)
print("Cohort BMI:", bmi)
print(
    f"type={type(bmi).__name__}, shape={bmi.shape}, "
    f"dtype={bmi.dtype}, nbytes={bmi.nbytes}"
)
Expected Output:
List * 2:  [64.5, 54.6, 64.5, 54.6]
Array * 2: [129.  109.2]
Cohort BMI: [22.85 22.44 22.86 25.06]
type=ndarray, shape=(4,), dtype=float64, nbytes=32
Notice two crucial differences immediately:

Operator semantics: Multiplying a Python list by 2 concatenates the list onto itself ([64.5, 54.6, 64.5, 54.6]). Multiplying a NumPy ndarray by 2 performs true mathematical scalar multiplication ([129.0, 109.2]).
Compact memory: Four float64 numbers take exactly 4 * 8 = 32 raw bytes (nbytes=32) with no per-element pointer overhead.




16.3.2 Shapes, Axes (axis=0 vs. axis=1) & Dtypes
# 3 districts (rows, axis=0) x 4 weeks (columns, axis=1)
cases = np.array([
    [12, 25, 40, 23],  # Dhaka
    [30, 15, 10,  5],  # Sylhet
    [ 5,  8, 12, 20],  # Khulna
])

print("shape:", cases.shape, "| ndim:", cases.ndim, "| dtype:", cases.dtype)
print("Total per district (axis=1):", np.sum(cases, axis=1))
print("Weekly mean (axis=0):       ", np.round(np.mean(cases, axis=0), 2))
print("Peak week index (axis=1):   ", np.argmax(cases, axis=1))

# Homogeneous dtype upcasting: mixing int + float promotes to float64
mixed = np.array([10, 11.5, 12])
print("Upcast mixed dtype:         ", mixed.dtype, mixed)
Expected Output:
shape: (3, 4) | ndim: 2 | dtype: int64
Total per district (axis=1): [100  60  45]
Weekly mean (axis=0):        [15.67 16.   20.67 16.  ]
Peak week index (axis=1):    [2 0 3]
Upcast mixed dtype:          float64 [10.  11.5 12. ]
Verify the axis rule on this rectangular (3, 4) dengue surveillance matrix:

np.sum(cases, axis=1) collapses the 4 week columns into 3 district totals ([100, 60, 45]).
np.mean(cases, axis=0) collapses the 3 district rows into 4 weekly means ([15.67, 16.0, 20.67, 16.0]).
np.argmax(cases, axis=1) returns the 0-based column index of each district’s peak week ([2, 0, 3], i.e., Week 3 for Dhaka, Week 1 for Sylhet, Week 4 for Khulna).




16.3.3 The View-vs-Copy Trap (Slicing Shares Memory!)
readings = np.array([10.4, 11.2, 12.1, 13.0, 11.8])

# NumPy slice = VIEW (shares underlying C memory buffer!)
view_slice = readings[1:4]
safe_copy = readings[1:4].copy()

print("Shares memory (view)?", np.shares_memory(readings, view_slice))
print("Shares memory (copy)?", np.shares_memory(readings, safe_copy))

view_slice[0] = -1.0  # Silently mutates `readings[1]`!
print("Original after view edit:", readings)

safe_copy[0] = 99.0   # Does NOT touch `readings`
print("Original after copy edit:", readings)
Expected Output:
Shares memory (view)? True
Shares memory (copy)? False
Original after view edit: [10.4 -1.  12.1 13.  11.8]
Original after copy edit: [10.4 -1.  12.1 13.  11.8]
Slicing returns a zero-copy view so NumPy can window across multi-gigabyte tensors instantly without blowing up RAM. That performance gift becomes a subtle aliasing bug if you forget .copy() before mutating a slice!



16.3.4 Boolean Masking & Sentinel-Safe np.nanmean
raw_hb = np.array([10.4, 999.0, 11.8, np.nan, 10.6, 12.6])

# Always copy as float before inserting np.nan!
clean_hb = np.array(raw_hb, dtype=float, copy=True)
clean_hb[clean_hb == 999.0] = np.nan

print("np.mean(clean_hb):   ", np.mean(clean_hb))
print("np.nanmean(clean_hb):", round(float(np.nanmean(clean_hb)), 2))

anemic_mask = clean_hb < 11.0
print("Anemic mask:         ", anemic_mask)
print("Anemic count:        ", int(np.sum(anemic_mask)))
print("Raw input untouched: ", raw_hb)
Expected Output:
np.mean(clean_hb):    nan
np.nanmean(clean_hb): 11.35
Anemic mask:          [ True False False False  True False]
Anemic count:         2
Raw input untouched:  [ 10.4 999.   11.8   nan  10.6  12.6]
Three defensive patterns work together here:

Float copy first: Integer arrays (int64) cannot store IEEE-754 np.nan, so np.array(..., dtype=float, copy=True) solves both dtype safety and caller non-mutation in one line.
NaN-aware aggregation: Standard np.mean poisons the entire result into nan if even one cell is np.nan; np.nanmean skips NaNs cleanly.
Mask counting: Comparing clean_hb < 11.0 returns False for np.nan, and int(np.sum(anemic_mask)) counts True values in C speed (True == 1, False == 0).




16.3.5 Broadcasting Rules in Action
Broadcasting lets NumPy combine arrays of different shapes without physically duplicating data in memory. NumPy aligns shapes from the rightmost (trailing) dimension leftward. Two dimensions are compatible if and only if:

They are equal, OR
One of them is 1 (or missing on the left, treated as 1).











Expression

Right Shape
Result Shape
Why It Works / Fails




X - col_means
(3, 2)

(2,) pads to (1, 2); 1 stretches to 3
