title: Appendix B — Essential Mathematics, Biostatistics & Deep Learning Equations Refresher
section: B.5 Deep Learning & Research Evaluation Equations (Chapters 27–36)
text:
B.5 Deep Learning & Research Evaluation Equations (Chapters 27–36)

B.5.1 2-Layer MLP Backpropagation Chain Rule (Chapter 27)
For hidden pre-activation \(z^{[1]} = W^{[1]} x + b^{[1]}\), activation \(a^{[1]} = g(z^{[1]})\), output logit \(z^{[2]} = W^{[2]} a^{[1]} + b^{[2]}\), and binary probability \(\hat{p} = \sigma(z^{[2]})\) under BCE loss:
\[\delta^{[2]} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial z^{[2]}} = \hat{p} - y, \qquad \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial W^{[2]}} = \frac{1}{n} \delta^{[2]} (a^{[1]})^\top, \qquad \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial b^{[2]}} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \delta^{[2]}_i\]
\[\delta^{[1]} = \Bigl((W^{[2]})^\top \delta^{[2]}\Bigr) \odot g'(z^{[1]}), \qquad \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial W^{[1]}} = \frac{1}{n} \delta^{[1]} X^\top\]


B.5.2 Variance-Preserving Weight Initialization (Chapter 29)
\[\text{Xavier / Glorot (Tanh, Sigmoid): } \operatorname{Var}(W) = \frac{2}{n_{\text{in}} + n_{\text{out}}}, \qquad \text{He / Kaiming (ReLU): } \operatorname{Var}(W) = \frac{2}{n_{\text{in}}}\]


B.5.3 2D Convolution Output Shape Formula (Chapter 30)
For input height \(H\), padding \(P\), kernel size \(K\), dilation \(D\) (default \(D = 1\)), and stride \(S\):
\[H_{\text{out}} = \left\lfloor \frac{H + 2P - D(K - 1) - 1}{S} \right\rfloor + 1 \;\;\xrightarrow{\,D=1\,}\;\; H_{\text{out}} = \left\lfloor \frac{H + 2P - K}{S} \right\rfloor + 1\]


B.5.4 Scaled Dot-Product Attention & Low-Rank Adaptation (Chapter 32)
\[\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\right) V\]
where \(M_{ij} = 0\) for allowed positions and \(M_{ij} = -\infty\) for masked (padding or future causal) tokens. Dividing by \(\sqrt{d_k}\) restores unit dot-product variance (\(\operatorname{Var}(q \cdot k / \sqrt{d_k}) = 1\)), preventing softmax saturation.
Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes \(W_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and learns rank-\(r\) factors \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and \(B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\) (\(B = 0\) at step 0):
\[W_{\text{eff}} = W_0 + \Delta W = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{r} B A, \qquad \text{Trainable params} = r(d_{\text{in}} + d_{\text{out}}) \ll d_{\text{in}} d_{\text{out}}\]


B.5.5 Algorithmic Fairness, Distribution Drift & Clinical Utility (Chapters 34–36)
Subgroup Fairness Disparity Metrics across sensitive groups \(g \in \mathcal{G}\) (Chapter 34):
\[\Delta_{\text{DP}} = \max_{g} P(\hat{Y}=1 \mid G=g) - \min_{g} P(\hat{Y}=1 \mid G=g)\]
\[\Delta_{\text{TPR}} = \max_{g} \text{TPR}_g - \min_{g} \text{TPR}_g, \qquad \Delta_{\text{EO}} = \max\bigl(\Delta_{\text{TPR}},\; \Delta_{\text{FPR}}\bigr)\]
Population Stability Index (PSI) comparing reference baseline bin shares \(p_b\) to production/deployment shares \(q_b\) (Chapters 34–35):
\[\text{PSI} = \sum_{b=1}^{B} (q_b - p_b) \ln\!\left(\frac{q_b}{p_b}\right)\]

Drift Triage Thresholds: \(\text{PSI} < 0.10\) (stable distribution), \(0.10 \le \text{PSI} \le 0.25\) (moderate shift — investigate covariates), \(\text{PSI} > 0.25\) (major distribution drift — re-calibrate or retrain).

Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) Net Benefit at clinical decision threshold \(p_t \in (0, 1)\) (Chapters 34, 36):
\[\text{NB}(p_t) = \frac{\text{TP}}{N} - \frac{\text{FP}}{N}\left(\frac{p_t}{1 - p_t}\right), \qquad \text{NB}_{\text{Treat-All}}(p_t) = \pi - (1 - \pi)\left(\frac{p_t}{1 - p_t}\right)\]
where \(\pi\) is outcome prevalence and \(\text{NB}_{\text{Treat-None}} = 0\). A prediction model delivers clinical value at threshold \(p_t\) only when \(\text{NB}(p_t) > \max\bigl(0,\; \text{NB}_{\text{Treat-All}}(p_t)\bigr)\).

D.2 Spine Public Health Datasets Dictionary
Three realistic, public-health-inspired synthetic datasets accompany this curriculum from Chapter 1 through Chapter 36 so you can trace how the exact same data problems evolve from basic Python loops to calibrated ML and PyTorch models.

D.2.1 1. clinic_triage.csv (120 Rows, 11 Columns)

Domain: Upazila community clinic patient intake records across 6 districts.
Exact Columns: patient_id (UHC-0001–UHC-0120), district, age_years, sex (F/M), weight_kg, height_cm, temp_c, systolic_bp, hemoglobin_g_dl, fever_days, triage_priority (Routine: 64, Moderate: 56).
Data Quality & Quirks: Zero missing cells by design—serves as the clean anchor dataset for Parts I–III (BMI calculation, fever triage branching, CSV/JSON I/O, OOP PatientRecord classes) and introductory classification/regression benchmarks.



D.2.2 2. mch_survey_sample.csv (500 Rows, 12 Columns)

Domain: Demographic and Health Survey (DHS)-style Maternal & Child Health household survey spanning 8 divisions and 50 primary sampling clusters (cluster_id).
Exact Columns: household_id (MCH-00001–MCH-00500), cluster_id, division, residence, wealth_quintile (Poorest to Richest), maternal_age_years, anc_visits, maternal_hb_g_dl, maternal_anemia (0/1), child_haz, child_stunted (0/1), fully_vaccinated (0/1).
Deliberate Real-World Quirks:

residence contains mixed-case entry errors ('Rural': 345, 'Urban': 140, 'rural': 11, 'urban': 4) requiring .str.strip().str.title().
anc_visits encodes 8 “Don’t Know / Refused” responses using legacy survey sentinel code 999 (must be replaced with np.nan before averaging or modeling!).
maternal_hb_g_dl has 22 missing (NaN) laboratory readings requiring leakage-free imputation inside Scikit-Learn pipelines.
Clustered household structure (cluster_id) mandates GroupKFold / StratifiedGroupKFold in Parts V and VII.




D.2.3 3. epi_surveillance.csv (416 Rows, 8 Columns)

Domain: Weekly district-level infectious disease surveillance and meteorological panel (\(4\text{ districts} \times 2\text{ years [2024–2025]} \times 52\text{ epi-weeks} = 416\text{ rows}\)).
Exact Columns: year, epi_week (1–52), district (Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Rajshahi), population, rainfall_mm, mean_temp_c, dengue_cases, respiratory_cases.
Data Quality & Quirks: Zero missing values; displays strong seasonal monsoon peaks, lagged rainfall-to-dengue transmission, and cross-district population scale differences (requiring incidence normalization per \(100{,}000\) population, panel-safe .groupby("district").shift(), TimeSeriesSplit, and GRU/LSTM sequence windowing in Chapter 31).

title: Appendix E — References, Glossary of Key Terms & About the Author
section: E.2 Glossary of 40 Core Terms (A–Z)
text:
E.2 Glossary of 40 Core Terms (A–Z)








Term
Concise Definition
Primary Ch.




Ablation Study
Systematic removal of one feature group or model component at a time to measure its true contribution to performance.
33


Adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR)
Odds ratio estimated from a multivariable logistic regression holding all other covariates constant.
20, 36


Aliasing
Two Python variable names pointing to the exact same mutable object in memory so mutating one mutates the other.
7


Autograd
PyTorch’s reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine that records tensor operations into a dynamic graph for .backward().
28


Backpropagation
Applying the multivariable chain rule backward from scalar loss to every weight tensor to compute exact gradients.
27


Batch Normalization
Layer normalizing activations across each mini-batch during training and using running population stats during .eval().
29


Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR)
Step-up multiple-testing procedure controlling the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses.
20


Bias-Variance Tradeoff
Tension between underfitting (high bias, overly rigid model) and overfitting (high variance, memorizing training noise).
21


Big-O Notation
Asymptotic upper bound describing how an algorithm’s runtime or memory grows as input size \(n\) increases.
11


Bootstrap Confidence Interval
Nonparametric uncertainty interval formed by resampling observations with replacement \(B\) times.
33


Brier Score
Mean squared error between predicted probabilities and binary outcomes; measures both calibration and discrimination.
23, 34


Broadcasting
NumPy/PyTorch rule aligning trailing array dimensions of size \(1\) without copying data in memory.
16


Calibration (ECE)
Agreement between predicted probabilities and observed event frequencies; summarized by Expected Calibration Error.
23, 34


Causal Attention Mask
Lower-triangular mask setting future token attention logits to \(-\infty\) so autoregressive models cannot peek ahead.
32


ColumnTransformer
Scikit-Learn meta-transformer routing numeric and categorical columns through separate leak-free preprocessing pipelines.
26


Copy-on-Write (CoW)
Pandas 3.x memory discipline preventing chained-assignment bugs by ensuring slices never silently mutate parent DataFrames.
17, 18


Covariate Shift (PSI)
Change in input feature distributions between training and deployment, quantified by Population Stability Index.
34


Cross-Entropy (Log-Loss)
Proper scoring rule penalizing confident wrong probability predictions logarithmically.
23, 27


Data Leakage
Contamination of training or preprocessing statistics (scaling, imputation, target encoding) by validation/test information.
21, 26


Decision Curve Analysis
Vickers-Elkin framework quantifying clinical Net Benefit of a prediction model across decision thresholds vs. Treat-All/None.
36


Dropout
Regularizer randomly zeroing neuron activations during model.train() and turning off automatically in model.eval().
29


Early Stopping
Halting neural training when validation loss fails to improve for patience epochs and restoring the best state_dict.
29


Equal Opportunity Gap
Maximum difference in True Positive Rate (sensitivity) across protected or demographic subgroups.
34


Gradient Clipping
Rescaling the global parameter gradient norm to \(\le \text{max\_norm}\) to prevent exploding updates in RNNs and deep MLPs.
29, 31


GroupKFold
Cross-validation splitter guaranteeing all rows from the same patient, hospital, or DHS cluster stay in a single fold.
21, 26


Hash Table
Key-value structure (dict, set) providing \(O(1)\) average lookup time by hashing keys to bucket addresses.
8, 11


Hidden State (Notebook)
Stale variables left in Jupyter kernel RAM from deleted or out-of-order cells that break Restart & Run All.
13


LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning freezing base weight \(W_0\) and learning a tiny rank-\(r\) update \(\Delta W = \frac{\alpha}{r}BA\).
32


McNemar’s Test
Exact paired nonparametric hypothesis test comparing discordant errors of two classifiers on the exact same test set.
33


Model Card
Structured documentation specifying a model’s intended use, training cohort, subgroup metrics, and clinical limitations.
35


Nested Cross-Validation
Two-loop CV separating inner hyperparameter selection from outer unbiased generalization estimation.
26


Permutation Importance
Model-agnostic importance measuring test-set metric drop when one feature column is randomly shuffled.
24


PR-AUC
Area under the Precision-Recall curve; far more informative than ROC-AUC under severe class imbalance.
23


Regularization (\(L_1\) / \(L_2\))
Penalty on coefficient magnitude (Lasso \(L_1\) drives sparsity; Ridge \(L_2\) shrinks correlated weights smoothly).
22


Residual Connection
Identity shortcut \(y = F(x) + x\) letting gradients flow unobstructed through deep CNNs and Transformers.
30, 32


Scaled Dot-Product Attention
Core Transformer weighting \(\operatorname{softmax}(QK^\top / \sqrt{d_k})V\) connecting every token to every relevant context token.
32


SHA-256 Manifest
Cryptographic 64-character hex fingerprint proving a dataset or model artifact has not changed by a single byte.
15, 35


Shapley Value (SHAP)
Game-theoretic attribution dividing a single prediction’s deviation from baseline fairly across all input features.
24


TRIPOD+AI
International reporting guideline ensuring transparent, reproducible clinical prediction model manuscripts.
35


Youden’s \(J\) Statistic
Classification threshold criterion maximizing \(\text{Sensitivity} + \text{Specificity} - 1\) on the ROC curve.
23, 34

section: E.3 About the Author
text:
E.3 About the Author
Mezanur Rahman Sharukh is an M.Sc. Statistician and Public Health & Machine Learning Researcher whose work bridges classical biostatistics, survey epidemiology, and reproducible machine learning engineering. His research focuses on maternal and child health disparities, infectious disease surveillance, probability calibration, subgroup fairness in clinical prediction models, and open-source educational tooling for quantitative researchers in low- and middle-income settings.
From First Line to First Paper was written to close the gap between introductory Python tutorials that stop at toy syntax and graduate machine learning papers that assume years of undocumented software engineering fluency. Every dataset, diagnostic check, and notebook in this curriculum was built so a dedicated learner with nothing more than a browser and Google Colab can progress systematically from their very first print() statement to a peer-review-ready, cryptographically verified research artifact.
